### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1. · a) — 1 mark

> At home

- **Answer: At home we can save water and electricity, plant trees and look after plants, put waste in the dustbin, reuse and recycle things, and say no to plastic.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): One or more sensible, specific ways to protect nature in this place (2 ways is ideal for the three printed lines).
  - partial (0.5 marks): A vague answer ("keep it clean", "be good to nature") with no specific action.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing sensible, or an answer unrelated to protecting nature.
- Model answer: At home I switch off lights and fans when not in use, close the tap while brushing, and water the plants.
- Marking guide: Open answer about what we can do at home to protect nature. Any one or two sensible ways get the mark, for example: Save water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse water for plants; Save electricity: switch off lights and fans; Grow and water plants / a kitchen or herbal garden; Separate wet and dry waste, compost kitchen waste, use the dustbin; Say no to plastic; use cloth bags; reuse and recycle; reduce paper waste. The textbook activity (Ch 4, p.12) leaves this open.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.12 l.1-6; p.10 l.22-26; p.11 l.1-5
- Teacher note: The four printed prompts (At home, At school, In parks, In our locality) appear only as the captions of the four pictures; the captions are used as the questions here. Answers are personal, so mark with the rubric.

### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1. · b) — 1 mark

> At school

- **Answer: At school we can plant and water trees, keep the classroom and campus clean, use dustbins, save paper, water and electricity, and spread awareness about saving plants.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): One or more sensible, specific ways to protect nature in this place (2 ways is ideal for the three printed lines).
  - partial (0.5 marks): A vague answer ("keep it clean", "be good to nature") with no specific action.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing sensible, or an answer unrelated to protecting nature.
- Model answer: At school we keep our classroom clean, use both sides of paper, and take care of the school garden.
- Marking guide: Open answer about what we can do at school to protect nature. Any one or two sensible ways get the mark, for example: Keep the classroom and campus clean; use dustbins; Save paper (use both sides, reduce paper waste); Switch off fans and lights; close taps; Plant trees / look after the school garden; Hold a clean-up drive or an awareness drive; say no to plastic. The textbook activity (Ch 4, p.12) leaves this open.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.12 l.1-6; p.10 l.22-26; p.11 l.1-5

### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1. · c) — 1 mark

> In parks

- **Answer: In parks we should not pluck flowers or break branches, throw litter only in dustbins, keep food and water for birds, plant trees, and take part in clean-up drives.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): One or more sensible, specific ways to protect nature in this place (2 ways is ideal for the three printed lines).
  - partial (0.5 marks): A vague answer ("keep it clean", "be good to nature") with no specific action.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing sensible, or an answer unrelated to protecting nature.
- Model answer: In parks we should not pluck flowers or litter, and we should keep water for birds.
- Marking guide: Open answer about what we can do in parks to protect nature. Any one or two sensible ways get the mark, for example: Do not pluck flowers or break plants; do not write on trees; Throw waste only in dustbins; do not litter; Keep food and water for birds; do not disturb animals; Plant trees; water plants; Join a clean-up drive. The textbook activity (Ch 4, p.12) leaves this open.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.12 l.1-6; p.10 l.22-26; p.11 l.1-5

### ⚑ Section 2 · Q11. · 2. — 1 mark

> \_\_\_\_\_\_ is a tree whose leaves are used to repel insects.

- **Answer: Neem**
- Also accept: neem · Neem · neem tree · the neem tree · neem leaves · nim · neemb · margosa · vepa · vembu · bevu · kadu limbu · limdo · Indian lilac · tulsi
- Marking guide: Neem: earthen pots were lined with neem leaves to keep insects and pests away from stored grain (and neem oil keeps mosquitoes away). Tulsi is also used at home to keep insects away, so a child who writes tulsi may be given the mark; the expected answer is neem.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.5 l.4-7; p.7 l.3-5
- Teacher note: The textbook answer is neem. Tulsi (holy basil) leaves are also commonly used to repel insects, so it is accepted; that is why this item is ⚑.

### ⚑ Section 4 · Q1V. · d) — 1 mark

> Reena and Amit were excited about a family trip, to a forest near their village.

- **Answer: True · False — corrected: the trip was to their village near a forest**
- Marking guide: Accept True or False. The textbook says they were excited about a family trip to "their village near a forest". A child who reads the sentence as "they were excited about a family trip" writes True; a child who notices that the trip was to the village (near a forest), not to a forest near the village, writes False. Both readings are defensible.

- Teacher note: Printed with a stray comma ("family trip, to a forest near their village") and the places swapped compared with the textbook ("their village near a forest"). Kept as printed; both True and False get the mark.

### ⚑ Section 5 · V. · 1. — 1 mark

> Who are Jenu Kurubas?

- **Answer: The Jenu Kurubas are a tribe from Karnataka. Their name comes from "Jenu", which means honey. They collect honey and sing songs to apologise to the bees, which shows their respect for nature.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Says they are a tribe (from Karnataka) AND links them to honey (honey collectors / name means honey / sing to the bees).
  - partial (0.5 marks): Only one part: "a tribe" or "they collect honey".
  - none (0 marks): Wrong or blank.
- Model answer: The Jenu Kurubas are a tribe from Karnataka who collect honey. They sing songs to say sorry to the bees.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.6 l.2-14

### ⚑ Section 5 · V. · 3. — 1 mark

- Also accept: blackbuck · black buck · mithun · gayal · one-horned rhinoceros · rhinoceros · rhino · gaur · Indian bison · bison · wild water buffalo · wild buffalo · Asiatic lion · lion · snow leopard · elephant · Asian elephant · Indian elephant · haathi · barasingha · swamp deer · Indian giant squirrel · giant squirrel · shekru · Malabar giant squirrel · sangai · brow-antlered deer · clouded leopard · serow · sambar · sambar deer · camel · chinkara · red panda · Nilgiri tahr · tahr · spotted deer · chital · deer · Phayre's leaf monkey · Phayre's langur · langur · alpine musk deer · musk deer · kasturi mrig · fishing cat · nilgai · blue bull · hangul · Kashmir stag · dugong
- Marking guide: Open: the answer depends on the state the child lives in. The parent checks it against their own state. State animals: Andhra Pradesh: blackbuck; Arunachal Pradesh: mithun; Assam: one-horned rhinoceros; Bihar: gaur; Chhattisgarh: wild water buffalo; Goa: gaur; Gujarat: Asiatic lion; Haryana: blackbuck; Himachal Pradesh: snow leopard; Jharkhand: elephant; Karnataka: elephant; Kerala: elephant; Madhya Pradesh: barasingha; Maharashtra: Indian giant squirrel (shekru); Manipur: sangai; Meghalaya: clouded leopard; Mizoram: serow; Nagaland: mithun; Odisha: sambar; Punjab: blackbuck; Rajasthan: camel (domestic) / chinkara (wild); Sikkim: red panda; Tamil Nadu: Nilgiri tahr; Telangana: spotted deer (chital); Tripura: Phayre's leaf monkey; Uttar Pradesh: barasingha (swamp deer); Uttarakhand: alpine musk deer; West Bengal: fishing cat; Delhi: nilgai; Jammu and Kashmir: hangul; Ladakh: snow leopard. ### ⚑ Section 8 · V111. · 1. — 2 marks

> Bamboo baskets were coated with cow dung on the outside.

- **Answer: Bamboo baskets were coated with cow dung on the outside so that the grains stored in them stay protected from insects and pests.**
- Answer points:
  - The baskets were used to store grains (1 mark)
  - The cow dung coating keeps insects and pests away / protects the grains (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Says the baskets store grain AND the cow dung protects the grain from insects and pests.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part: "to keep insects away" or "to store grains safely", or a sensible other reason (to seal gaps, keep out moisture).
  - none (0 marks): Wrong or blank.
- Model answer: The baskets were used to store grains. The cow dung coating keeps insects and pests away, so the grains stay safe.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.5 l.2-7

### ⚑ Section 8 · V111. · 2. — 2 marks

> If we overuse wood from nature,

- **Answer: If we overuse wood from nature, our forests will deplete (get used up). Trees will be cut down, and animals and birds will lose their homes.**
- Answer points:
  - Forests will deplete / trees will be cut down and get used up (1 mark)
  - A sensible further effect: animals and birds lose their homes, less rain or fresh air, soil erosion, pollution, no wood for the future (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Completes the sentence sensibly: forests deplete / trees are cut down, plus one further effect (animals lose homes, less rain, soil erosion, less fresh air, no wood left for later).
  - partial (1 mark): Only one sensible effect, e.g. "forests will finish".
  - none (0 marks): No sensible consequence.
- Model answer: If we overuse wood from nature, our forests will deplete, and animals and birds will lose their homes.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.11 l.17-20
- Teacher note: Printed as an incomplete sentence ending with a comma, under "Give reasons". The child completes it with the result; the textbook example is "our forests deplete". Accept any sensible completion.

Maharashtra: the large state in the west on the Arabian Sea coast, south of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, north of Goa and Karnataka, west of Chhattisgarh and Telangana; Mumbai is on its coast. 1 mark if the right region is marked and named (any spelling); ½ if it is marked in the right area but overlaps a neighbour.

## All items

### Section 1 — 1. How can we protect the natural environment around us? (4 marks)

**Q1. — How can we protect the natural environment around us? (4x1=4)**

*Picture: Pictures 1 to 4 for parts a) to d)*

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1. · a) — 1 mark

> At home

- **Answer: At home we can save water and electricity, plant trees and look after plants, put waste in the dustbin, reuse and recycle things, and say no to plastic.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): One or more sensible, specific ways to protect nature in this place (2 ways is ideal for the three printed lines).
  - partial (0.5 marks): A vague answer ("keep it clean", "be good to nature") with no specific action.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing sensible, or an answer unrelated to protecting nature.
- Model answer: At home I switch off lights and fans when not in use, close the tap while brushing, and water the plants.
- Marking guide: Open answer about what we can do at home to protect nature. Any one or two sensible ways get the mark, for example: Save water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse water for plants; Save electricity: switch off lights and fans; Grow and water plants / a kitchen or herbal garden; Separate wet and dry waste, compost kitchen waste, use the dustbin; Say no to plastic; use cloth bags; reuse and recycle; reduce paper waste. The textbook activity (Ch 4, p.12) leaves this open.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.12 l.1-6; p.10 l.22-26; p.11 l.1-5
- Teacher note: The four printed prompts (At home, At school, In parks, In our locality) appear only as the captions of the four pictures; the captions are used as the questions here. Answers are personal, so mark with the rubric.

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1. · b) — 1 mark

> At school

- **Answer: At school we can plant and water trees, keep the classroom and campus clean, use dustbins, save paper, water and electricity, and spread awareness about saving plants.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): One or more sensible, specific ways to protect nature in this place (2 ways is ideal for the three printed lines).
  - partial (0.5 marks): A vague answer ("keep it clean", "be good to nature") with no specific action.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing sensible, or an answer unrelated to protecting nature.
- Model answer: At school we keep our classroom clean, use both sides of paper, and take care of the school garden.
- Marking guide: Open answer about what we can do at school to protect nature. Any one or two sensible ways get the mark, for example: Keep the classroom and campus clean; use dustbins; Save paper (use both sides, reduce paper waste); Switch off fans and lights; close taps; Plant trees / look after the school garden; Hold a clean-up drive or an awareness drive; say no to plastic. The textbook activity (Ch 4, p.12) leaves this open.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.12 l.1-6; p.10 l.22-26; p.11 l.1-5

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1. · c) — 1 mark

> In parks

- **Answer: In parks we should not pluck flowers or break branches, throw litter only in dustbins, keep food and water for birds, plant trees, and take part in clean-up drives.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): One or more sensible, specific ways to protect nature in this place (2 ways is ideal for the three printed lines).
  - partial (0.5 marks): A vague answer ("keep it clean", "be good to nature") with no specific action.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing sensible, or an answer unrelated to protecting nature.
- Model answer: In parks we should not pluck flowers or litter, and we should keep water for birds.
- Marking guide: Open answer about what we can do in parks to protect nature. Any one or two sensible ways get the mark, for example: Do not pluck flowers or break plants; do not write on trees; Throw waste only in dustbins; do not litter; Keep food and water for birds; do not disturb animals; Plant trees; water plants; Join a clean-up drive. The textbook activity (Ch 4, p.12) leaves this open.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.12 l.1-6; p.10 l.22-26; p.11 l.1-5

#### ⚑ Section 1 · Q1. · d) — 1 mark

> In our locality

- **Answer: In our locality we can plant trees, organise a clean-up drive, keep the streets and water bodies clean, say no to plastic, keep water for birds and animals, and spread awareness about protecting nature.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): One or more sensible, specific ways to protect nature in this place (2 ways is ideal for the three printed lines).
  - partial (0.5 marks): A vague answer ("keep it clean", "be good to nature") with no specific action.
  - none (0 marks): Nothing sensible, or an answer unrelated to protecting nature.
- Model answer: In our locality we can plant trees, organise a clean-up drive and say no to plastic.
- Marking guide: Open answer about what we can do in our locality to protect nature. Any one or two sensible ways get the mark, for example: Plant trees along the roads; Organise a clean-up drive; keep streets, ponds and rivers clean; Say no to plastic; do not burn waste; Keep food and water for birds and stray animals; Spread awareness about saving plants. The textbook activity (Ch 4, p.12) leaves this open.

#### ⚑ Section 2 · Q11. · 2. — 1 mark

- Also accept: neem · Neem · neem tree · the neem tree · neem leaves · nim · neemb · margosa · vepa · vembu · bevu · kadu limbu · limdo · Indian lilac · tulsi
- Marking guide: Neem: earthen pots were lined with neem leaves to keep insects and pests away from stored grain (and neem oil keeps mosquitoes away). Tulsi is also used at home to keep insects away, so a child who writes tulsi may be given the mark; the expected answer is neem.

- Marking guide: Textbook table: Hari Jiroti — fruit-bearing trees — plantation. Accept any close spelling. Van Mahotsav (the tree-planting festival) is a sensible answer from general knowledge and is accepted.

### Section 3 — 111. Match the following. (5 marks)

**Q111. — Match the following. (5x1=5)**

#### Section 3 · Q111. — 5 marks

> Match the following.

- Pairs:
  - a) Tumri → a traditional way of preserving grains in Uttarakhand
  - b) Neem oil → to keep mosquitoes away
  - c) Nagada → a type of drum (instrument)
  - d) Vat Purnima → worshipping the banyan tree
  - e) Solar panels → generate electricity for fans, bulbs etc.
- **Answer: a) Tumri – a traditional way of preserving grains in Uttarakhand; b) Neem oil – to keep mosquitoes away; c) Nagada – a type of drum (instrument); d) Vat Purnima – worshipping the banyan tree; e) Solar panels – generate electricity for fans, bulbs etc.**
- Answer points:
  - a) Tumri – a traditional way of preserving grains in Uttarakhand (Ch 4, p.6 l.24-27) (1 mark)
  - b) Neem oil – to keep mosquitoes away (p.7 l.3-5) (1 mark)
  - c) Nagada – a type of drum (instrument) (p.8 l.6-7) (1 mark)
  - d) Vat Purnima – worshipping the banyan tree (p.10 l.10-11) (1 mark)
  - e) Solar panels – generate electricity for fans, bulbs etc. (p.2 l.22-24) (1 mark)
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.2 l.22-24; p.6 l.24-27; p.7 l.3-5; p.8 l.6-7; p.10 l.10-11

#### ⚑ Section 4 · Q1V. · d) — 1 mark

**V. — Answer the following. (5x1=5)**

#### ⚑ Section 5 · V. · 1. — 1 mark

> Who are Jenu Kurubas?

- **Answer: The Jenu Kurubas are a tribe from Karnataka. Their name comes from "Jenu", which means honey. They collect honey and sing songs to apologise to the bees, which shows their respect for nature.**
- Rubric:
  - full (1 mark): Says they are a tribe (from Karnataka) AND links them to honey (honey collectors / name means honey / sing to the bees).
  - partial (0.5 marks): Only one part: "a tribe" or "they collect honey".
  - none (0 marks): Wrong or blank.

#### ⚑ Section 5 · V. · 2. — 1 mark

#### ⚑ Section 5 · V. · 5. — 1 mark

  - partial (0.5 marks): Says only "we love plants and animals" or "it is our tradition" without respect/protection of nature.

### Section 8 — V111. Give reasons for the following. (4 marks)

**V111. — Give reasons for the following. (2x2=4)**

#### ⚑ Section 8 · V111. · 1. — 2 marks

> Bamboo baskets were coated with cow dung on the outside.

- **Answer: Bamboo baskets were coated with cow dung on the outside so that the grains stored in them stay protected from insects and pests.**
- Answer points:
  - The baskets were used to store grains (1 mark)
  - The cow dung coating keeps insects and pests away / protects the grains (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Says the baskets store grain AND the cow dung protects the grain from insects and pests.
  - partial (1 mark): Only one part: "to keep insects away" or "to store grains safely", or a sensible other reason (to seal gaps, keep out moisture).
  - none (0 marks): Wrong or blank.
- Model answer: The baskets were used to store grains. The cow dung coating keeps insects and pests away, so the grains stay safe.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.5 l.2-7

#### ⚑ Section 8 · V111. · 2. — 2 marks

> If we overuse wood from nature,

- **Answer: If we overuse wood from nature, our forests will deplete (get used up). Trees will be cut down, and animals and birds will lose their homes.**
- Answer points:
  - Forests will deplete / trees will be cut down and get used up (1 mark)
  - A sensible further effect: animals and birds lose their homes, less rain or fresh air, soil erosion, pollution, no wood for the future (1 mark)
- Rubric:
  - full (2 marks): Completes the sentence sensibly: forests deplete / trees are cut down, plus one further effect (animals lose homes, less rain, soil erosion, less fresh air, no wood left for later).
  - partial (1 mark): Only one sensible effect, e.g. "forests will finish".
  - none (0 marks): No sensible consequence.
- Model answer: If we overuse wood from nature, our forests will deplete, and animals and birds will lose their homes.
- Source: Ch 4 (deev104), p.11 l.17-20
- Teacher note: Printed as an incomplete sentence ending with a comma, under "Give reasons". The child completes it with the result; the textbook example is "our forests deplete". Accept any sensible completion.
